answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks from trusted seeds, assigning votes by reachable, independently supported paths. A sybil cluster can add internal links, but its sparse external cut has low conductance, so little walk probability enters from outside. With per-node influence capped, min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore limit its aggregate voting weight; pulse, sparrow, and quartz may label test attestations without changing that bound.
